champion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy
ordered_diagnoses: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain, and muscle weakness with elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin
salient_findings: Mild weakness in bilateral hip flexor muscles
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase) and bilirubin
key_facts: 71-year-old man presented with three weeks of jaundice
Weight loss and abdominal pain reported
Bilateral lower-extremity weakness, most noticeable when arising from a chair
No history of autoimmune or neuromuscular conditions
Taking atorvastatin as a home medication
Epigastric tenderness without guarding or rebound on physical examination
Significant elevation in creatinine kinase (CK) level
CT abdomen/pelvis showed a 2.6 × 3.1 cm pancreatic head mass
MRI showed diffuse myositis affecting lower extremities
Pancreatic head biopsy was hypocellular with scant atypical cells
Biliary stricture biopsy was consistent with adenocarcinoma

s4.champion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy

raw.champion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain, and a pancreatic head mass on CT, along with a biliary stricture biopsy consistent with adenocarcinoma, strongly suggests pancreatic cancer. The significant elevation in creatinine kinase (CK) level and MRI findings of diffuse myositis affecting lower extremities, in the absence of a history of autoimmune or neuromuscular conditions, point towards a paraneoplastic syndrome, specifically paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy, associated with the pancreatic cancer.

rejected.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has pancreatic adenocarcinoma, this diagnosis alone does not explain the muscle weakness and elevated CK levels.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyolysis
rejected.why: Rhabdomyolysis is a possible consequence of the patient's condition but does not account for the underlying cause of the pancreatic mass and the paraneoplastic syndrome.

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence pointing towards cholangiocarcinoma, and the biliary stricture biopsy was consistent with adenocarcinoma, which is more suggestive of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Statins-induced myopathy
rejected.why: While the patient is taking atorvastatin, the presence of a pancreatic head mass and the biopsy results indicating adenocarcinoma suggest that the myopathy is more likely paraneoplastic rather than statin-induced.
